report.summary: Parsed chunk 1 of slice.py: docstring, imports, and 5 public+private functions. Claims about token counting, skeleton behavior, and reverse edges are uncheckable; docstring claims about module purpose are kept.
risks: _whole_repo_tokens | low | Fallback heuristic (chars//4) may produce flattering reduction ratios when total_tokens absent. | Check if index always includes total_tokens in current codebase.
_skeleton | medium | For non-document files with no extractable units, fallback emits up to 12 lines which may be misleading. | Verify that such fallback is acceptable and documented elsewhere.
_reverse_edges | medium | Function defined but incomplete in chunk; may not be fully implemented. | Review complete implementation in later chunks.
todos: Verify that estimate_tokens actually calls count_tokens from .tokens (imported).
Check that _read uses root/rel correctly when root is Path.
Confirm that _skeleton's docstring claim about 'never larger than raw document' holds for code units.

claims.text: slice_tokens (the numerator) is tokenizer-exact whenever tiktoken is installed, but this used to be total_chars // 4 unconditionally -- a real token count divided by a heuristic one, which makes the headline reduction % wrong by however far chars/4 misses on this corpus (it under-counts source code, so the published number was systematically flattering). total_tokens is now carried through the index by the same tokenizer.
claims.why: The function only reads total_tokens from index; the claim about historical behavior and tokenizer accuracy cannot be verified from this code alone.

claims.text: The fallback survives for index dicts that predate the field: an older JSON dump, or the Rust engine (structcore-rs emits total_chars only). Degraded is allowed; degraded-and-silent is not, hence the returned flag, which callers surface as whole_repo_tokens_exact.
claims.why: The function indeed uses total_chars // 4 as fallback and returns exact_flag=False.

claims.text: Editable units of a file: code units, or -- for a document -- SECTIONS.
claims.why: The function returns list of sections for documents (via markdown_mod.parse_document) or code units (via extract_units).

claims.text: A DocSection is field-compatible with a CodeUnit (module/name/line/end_line/loc/source/language), so a caller that already handles units needs no type switch.
claims.why: The definition of DocSection and CodeUnit is not in this chunk; field compatibility cannot be verified.

claims.text: What a caller MUST NOT do is feed sections into the call-graph approximation: identifiers in prose are not calls, and semantic_slice keeps the two apart for that reason.
claims.why: No call-graph approximation or semantic_slice code present in this chunk.

claims.text: Signature-level digest of a file: one line per unit (its first line).
claims.why: The function iterates over units and outputs first non-empty line truncated to 120 chars per unit.

claims.text: For a DOCUMENT the analogue is exact and is delegated to markdown.document_skeleton: the heading tree is the signature set, the prose is the body, the body is dropped, and the drop is reported inline.
claims.why: The function calls markdown_mod.document_skeleton; its behavior (dropping body, reporting drop) is not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: That path also carries the hard invariant this function cannot state for code -- the result is never larger than the raw document.
claims.why: The invariant is claimed for document_skeleton, which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Routing documents here matters as much as what it produces. The old fallthrough (spec_for returns None for .md, so zero units, so the len(out) == 1 branch) emitted twelve raw lines of prose under a header reading (skeleton) -- presenting a document as though it had signatures, with no statement that the other 3,580 lines existed at all.
claims.why: The function now checks doc_spec_for first and delegates to document_skeleton, avoiding the described fallthrough. The len(out)==1 branch still exists for code files with no extractable units.
